prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 243, X-ray timing on the counts contract (tranche T4 by D-R10-232-01), the kernel, contract and gate part
document: X_RAY_COUNTS_GATE.md (the contract, the gate and the files requested) and HIGH_ENERGY.md (the kernel and the validation table), both written after this file
committed: before js/kernels/xray/*, the validator, the oracle scripts and their pinned results, the synthetic generator's output, any product file, any lesson, and before any count series, period, hardness or oracle output of Prompt 243 existed. Phase 1 of the session (reading the roadmap, the register, the checkpoint, the statistics kernel, js/measure/periodogram.js and the multi-messenger and radio patterns) preceded it and fixed nothing here from a result. No expected value below is the output of the kernel: every one is either a closed form checked once with an independent script (the literals of A1 and A2), arithmetic written in the leg, or a bound set by a stated discretisation or by the Monte Carlo error of a stated ensemble.
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied) is NOT RUN and says why. No published number, product identifier, catalogue value, band definition, licence term or citation detail is typed anywhere from memory: every authentic fact comes from a file Carl supplied under tests/fixtures/xray/authentic/, with its source, its terms as read and its retrieval date in that directory's SOURCES.json; a product that was not retrieved is rights basis C and nothing of it ships. Counts are integers and every error bar on a count or a rate is a Poisson interval (never a Gaussian one, never sqrt(N)); a hardness ratio carries a Poisson-based interval; a period is never reported without a significance by simulation and the number of simulations, and the asymptotic false-alarm formula of js/measure/periodogram.js is not used for it; a series without good-time intervals is refused by every entry point; a period search on times that are not stated barycentric is refused; a candidate period at the sampling's alias is flagged and never reported as clean. Every record computed from a synthetic series carries synthetic: true and the series' label.

seeds.design: xr-243-design (used only to build and debug; never in a leg)
seeds.note: A stream is stream('noise', seed, label) of js/random/streams.js; each leg names its seeds and labels below. The Poisson sampler is exact (inversion from the mode), never a Gaussian approximation.

scope.built: (1) the counts-series contract (gravitas.counts-series/1): time system and barycentric flag, bin starts and stops, exposure (live time) per bin, counts per energy band in the source region, background as a region (area ratio and counts) or a stated rate or declared negligible, the dead-time statement (folded into the exposure, or a fraction that must reproduce it), good-time intervals, the energy bands; every refusal by code; (2) the Poisson rate and its exact (Garwood) interval, and the net rate with a background region by a profile-likelihood interval; (3) binning by counts that conserves counts and exposure and never joins bins across a gap; (4) the hardness ratio (H - S) / (H + S) with an exact conditional-binomial interval on source-region counts and a profile interval for the background-subtracted form; (5) the hardness-intensity points; (6) outburst detection by a stated rule with a refusal when no quiet level exists; (7) the period search on unevenly sampled counts with gaps (the generalized Lomb-Scargle of js/measure/periodogram.js, weights from the constant-rate null), significance by simulation, a period interval by a parametric bootstrap, the alias flag and the periodic-background flag; (8) a labelled synthetic generator with a truth manifest.
scope.notBuilt: any real product (none was supplied; nothing was fetched); a pack; a catalogue subset; the period change of a pulsar; a pulse-profile or epoch-folding estimator; event-list input (the contract is for binned counts); a response-weighted hardness or a flux; a state classification of an X-ray binary; a mass function or a compact-object mass (the optical radial-velocity table of the prompt's third investigation is not requested: no recorded decision for one exists); any lesson, panel, model-page section or instructor material.

synthetic.label: SYNTHETIC COUNT SERIES: generated by js/kernels/xray/synthetic.js from the stated parameters and seed; the counts are Poisson draws of the stated rates, the good-time intervals, exposures and background are invented, and no X-ray source, product or archive is represented.

orbit.what: eight good-time intervals of 1200 s, one every 5760 s, bins of 40 s, a dead-time fraction of 0.1 (exposure 36 s), net source rates soft 0.30 and hard 0.20 c/s, background region rates soft 0.05 and hard 0.05 c/s at area ratio 0.25, 240 bins; searched over periods 150 s to 1500 s

dwell.what: 200 dwells of 10 s, one every 100 s (a bin is a dwell), exposure 10 s, net source rates soft 12 and hard 8 c/s, no background; searched over periods 20 s to 400 s

outburst.what: two good-time intervals [0, 30000] s and [32000, 60000] s, bins of 100 s with no dead time, a quiet net rate of 2 c/s (soft 1.2, hard 0.8), a fast-rise exponential-decay outburst starting at 12000 s with peak excess factor 10 and e-folding 4000 s: the rate is q (1 + 10 exp(-(t - 12000) / 4000)) for t >= 12000

hardness.what: one good-time interval of 30000 s, bins of 100 s, no dead time, no background, net rates soft 0.06 and hard 0.04 c/s (about 3000 counts), true hardness (0.04 - 0.06) / 0.10 = -0.2; the interval length is scaled to set the total counts in leg C1b

unevenNull.what: the scene of leg C4: 150 bins of 20 s in 6 good-time intervals of 500 s every 3000 s (25 bins each), no dead time, a constant total rate of 0.5 c/s in the source region, no background; searched over periods 60 s to 600 s

fields.time: {system, barycentric, epoch}: the time scale of the bin edges (one of TDB, TT, UTC, MET) and whether the edges are corrected to the solar-system barycentre (a boolean that must be stated)
fields.start, stop: the bin edges in seconds since the epoch, ordered and not overlapping
fields.exposure: live seconds per bin, 0 or more; a bin with exposure 0 has 0 counts and is not used
fields.bands: at least one energy band {id, lo, hi, unit}, ordered by energy and not overlapping; hardness needs two
fields.counts: per band, source region, integers of 0 or more
fields.background: {kind: 'region', areaRatio, counts per band, exposure optional} or {kind: 'rate', rate per band} or {kind: 'none', negligible: true}
fields.deadTime: {kind: 'in-exposure'} (the exposure is already live time) or {kind: 'fraction', fraction per bin} which must reproduce the exposure from the good-time overlap to 1e-6
fields.gti: good-time intervals [start, stop], ordered, positive length, not overlapping; every bin with exposure above 0 lies inside them and its exposure does not exceed its overlap with them by more than 1e-9 of the bin width

rules.rate: per bin, counts / exposure with the exact (Garwood) interval at every count, level 0.6827 unless stated
rules.net: N_s ~ Poisson(T (S + r B)), N_b ~ Poisson(T_b B), S >= 0: the interval of S is the set where the profile deviance (B profiled out) is at most the chi-square quantile on one degree of freedom at the level; the estimate is max(0, N_s / T - r N_b / T_b)
rules.hardness: HR = (H - S) / (H + S) of the source-region counts in the two stated bands; total form: the exact conditional-binomial (Clopper-Pearson) interval of p = H / (H + S) at the level, HR = 2 p - 1; net form: the profile deviance in HR with the two net rates and the two backgrounds profiled out, S >= 0
rules.binByCounts: greedy: consecutive bins are merged until the chosen band's source-region counts reach minCounts; a group never joins bins whose gap (start of the next minus stop of the previous) exceeds maxGap; the last group of a run that cannot reach minCounts is kept and flagged short
rules.outburst: q = the lower quartile of the rates over bins with exposure above 0 (the 25th percentile by linear interpolation; AM1); a bin is elevated when its Garwood lower bound at level 0.9973 exceeds factor * q (factor 3); a run is at least 3 consecutive elevated bins with gaps at most maxGap; if more than half of the live bins are elevated there is no quiet level and the search is refused (noQuietLevel)
rules.period: generalized Lomb-Scargle (js/measure/periodogram.js: floating mean, power the weighted variance fraction), t the bin midpoint, y = counts / exposure, weight proportional to exposure under the constant-rate null with rate lambda = total counts / total exposure; grid f = 1/maxPeriod + k df, df = 1 / (oversample T), T = the range of the midpoints, oversample 5, as the existing module; significance p = (1 + #{simulated maxima >= observed maximum}) / (nSim + 1) over the whole grid, each simulation Poisson(lambda * exposure_i) per bin; nSim at least 99 (default 999); minimum period at least twice the widest bin
rules.periodInterval: parametric bootstrap: 200 Poisson series from the best sinusoid plus floating mean, each searched in a window of plus and minus 2 frequency resolutions, the 0.6827 percentile interval of the periods
rules.alias: window W(f) = |sum w exp(2 pi i f t)|^2 / (sum w)^2 on the grid; a sampling frequency is a local maximum of W with W >= 0.25 and f >= 2 / T; delta = 1 / T; a candidate is flagged atSampling when it lies within delta of a sampling frequency, and aliasPair when another local maximum of the periodogram with power >= 0.8 of the highest has |f - f'| or f + f' within delta of a sampling frequency; both members of a pair are flagged
rules.backgroundPeriodic: the same search (nSim 199) on the background-region counts; flagged when p <= 0.01 and the best frequency is within 2 / T of the source's

The roadmap asks for a persistent source, a transient and a pulsar (two or three products from an all-sky monitor or NICER, public domain through HEASARC); the prompt's own words are the only product description used here.

dead-time statement (folded into the exposure or a fraction)

fillsRule.each requirement: filled only by a sentence or keyword in the product's own documentation or header, cited by file and line or keyword; 'the file has a column of that name' is not documentation

kernelVerdict.A: every non-period leg and every period leg passes: timing and hardness
kernelVerdict.B: every non-period leg passes and at least one period leg fails: light curves, rates, hardness and outbursts only; no period claims

verdictFunction.netForms: a background-subtracted rate or hardness may be claimed only if B5, B6, C3 and C3b all pass; otherwise the total-count forms only, said so; this does not change the kernel verdict

productVerdict.A: at least one authentic product fills every required item with barycentric times stated true, the kernel verdict is A, and E1 (the pulsar within the catalogue under the fixed contract) passes: timing and hardness on the products that fill the contract
productVerdict.B: at least one authentic product fills the required items except that its times are not stated barycentric, or the kernel verdict is B, or E1 is not run or fails: light curves and hardness only; no period claims; consumers: the outburst and hardness parts only

productVerdict.noProductSupplied: if no authentic product was supplied the product verdict is NOT ESTABLISHED and is treated as C for any statement about a real source; the kernel verdict on synthetic series is computed from the legs and stands alone

consumersRule.synthetic-only lesson: permitted only when the kernel verdict is A, every figure and sentence says SYNTHETIC and states the claim limits, and no statement is made about a real source; permitted for hardness and outbursts only when the kernel verdict is B
consumersRule.real-product lesson: permitted only when a product verdict of A or B exists with the product's terms page saved; period statements need A
consumersRule.lessons wait: no lesson, panel or model-page section is built by this prompt's first pull request regardless; they wait for Carl's go-ahead and for this rule

checks.what: the Poisson rate interval against closed forms of the exact (Garwood) interval: no counts in an exposure of 10 s at level 0.95 is [0, ln(40) / 10] (the upper end is -ln(0.025) / T); one count in 1 s has lower end -ln(0.975); the rate is counts over exposure exactly; the interval brackets the rate; the method label is 'poisson-garwood'; a non-integer, negative or missing count is refused with code 'counts' and a bad exposure with code 'exposure'

the hardness ratio against exact values: 30 hard and 10 soft counts give 0.5 and 10 and 10 give 0; swapping the bands negates the ratio and mirrors the interval to 1e-15; 0 hard of 10 total at level 0.95 has the interval [-1, -0.38300578436247834] and 10 hard of 10 has [0.38300578436247834, 1] (the exact binomial end 1 - 0.025^(1/10) = 0.30849710781876083 mapped by HR = 2 p - 1); 0 hard of 1 has the upper end 0.95 (p = 1 - 0.025); no counts in either band is refused with code 'noCounts'; the ratio lies in [-1, 1] and the interval inside it

binning by counts on the 'orbit' scene (seed 243001, label 'bin') into groups of at least 50 source-region counts in the soft plus hard bands with maxGap 25 s: total counts and total exposure are conserved (counts exactly, exposure to a relative 1e-12 of the sum); every group's members are consecutive bins; no group spans a gap above 25 s (so none crosses the 4560 s gap between good-time intervals); a group not flagged short has at least 50 counts and would have fewer without its last member; a group flagged short has fewer than 50; every output series passes the contract's own validation

period recovery on the 'orbit' scene over 20 seeds (243100 + k, label 'period', k = 0 to 19) with the sinusoid of 612.5 s and fractional semi-amplitude 0.3 on the net source rate (random phase from the seed): for every seed the best frequency lies within 0.25 / T of 1 / 612.5 (T the range of the bin midpoints), the significance by simulation (nSim 199) is at most 0.01, the result says method 'simulation' with nSim 199, and no 'falseAlarm' field is present

hardness recovery on the 'hardness' scene (about 3000 counts, true -0.2) at seeds 243001 to 243005 (label 'hr'): the pooled total-form interval at level 0.9973 contains -0.2 for all five and its half-width is at most 0.07; the hardness-intensity points made with minCounts equal to the total counts (one group) give one point whose hardness equals the pooled value to 1e-12

outburst detection on the 'outburst' scene (seed 243001, label 'burst'): exactly one run, its start within 100 s of 12000 s, its stop within 1000 s of the analytic end of the elevated phase 12000 + 4000 ln(5) = 18437.75 s (where q (1 + 10 e^-x/4000) = 3 q), the peak bin within one bin of the first bin of the run; on 20 constant-rate series of the same sampling (rate 2 c/s, seeds 243200 + k, label 'quiet') no run is reported; on the series with the rate multiplied by 6 from 8000 s to 50000 s (seed 243001, label 'high') the search is refused with code 'noQuietLevel'

the exact interval against scipy.stats.chi2.ppf (Python, no Gravitas code) at every count 0 to 300 and at 400 and 1000, exposures 1 and 37.5 s, levels 0.6827, 0.9545 and 0.95: lower and upper ends to a relative 1e-8 (an end of exactly 0 to 1e-15 absolute)

the hardness interval against scipy.stats.beta.ppf (the Clopper-Pearson ends, HR = 2 p - 1): every H from 0 to N for N in 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30 and H in 0, 1, N/10, N/2, N-1, N for N in 100 and 1000, levels 0.6827 and 0.95: both ends to 1e-9 absolute

the kernel's period power against astropy.timeseries.LombScargle (generalized, floating mean, standard normalization, method 'cython', dy = sqrt(lambda / exposure)) on the 'orbit' scene series of seed 243301 (label 'oracle', with the 612.5 s sinusoid): the power on the first 300 grid frequencies to 1e-9 absolute; the grid's first, last and length equal js/measure/periodogram.js's for the same times; and the kernel's best frequency equals the frequency that module's searchPeriod returns for the same times, values y and errors dy to a relative 1e-6 of the grid step

the simulated significance against an independent implementation (numpy matrix form of the same statistic, its own random generator, 19999 simulations) on six committed series of the 'orbit' scene (seeds 243401 to 243406, label 'sig'; fractional semi-amplitudes 0, 0, 0, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08 on the 612.5 s sinusoid): the kernel's p (nSim 999) and the oracle's differ by at most 4 sqrt(pbar (1 - pbar) (1 / 999 + 1 / 19999)) + 1 / 999, pbar their mean, for every series

the net-rate profile interval against scipy.optimize (brentq on the deviance, the nuisance rate maximised by minimize_scalar): twelve committed cases (N_s, N_b, T, T_b, r) at levels 0.6827 and 0.95 including N_s = 0, N_s < r N_b and N_s >> r N_b: both ends to a relative 1e-6 (an end at the S >= 0 bound exactly 0)

amendments.what: the rule as committed took q as the MEDIAN rate and refused when more than half of the live bins are elevated (above factor times q). With q the median that refusal can never fire: more than half of the bins above 3 times the median would put the median above 3 times itself. So the refusal clause, and the 'high' case of A6 that requires it, contradicted the rule's own definition of q. q becomes the lower quartile (25th percentile by linear interpolation of the sorted rates), which stays at the quiet level when up to about three quarters of a series is quiet and sits in the bright level only when more than three quarters of it is bright. The factor, the level, minBins, the refusal condition (more than half elevated) and every bound of A6 are unchanged. A specification slip found by reasoning about the rule before the validator existed, not a result.

leg (i) says the candidate is found at 0.007 or its reflection 0.003. On a series sampled once per 100 s every frequency k/100 +/- 0.007 (k = 0 to 5: 0.003, 0.007, 0.013, 0.017, 0.023, 0.027, ...) is an exact alias of the true one, with powers that differ only by the dwell's own smearing (a fraction of a percent to two percent) and by noise, so which alias is highest is not decided by the sampling. The leg's purpose is that the result is never reported clean, so (i) is read as: the candidate lies within 2 grid steps of one of the frequencies |k/100 +/- 0.007| (k = 0 to 5) inside the searched range, AND carries an aliasPair or atSampling flag, AND the result is not clean. The (ii) and (iii) clauses and the frequencies are unchanged. A specification slip found by reasoning about the sampling before the validator existed, not a result.
